name: Schulte Table
tagline: Browser trainer where you tap numbers in order on a grid while keeping your eyes fixed on the center, sold as speed reading and attention practice.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Tools in this category are usually free or ad supported, so there may be nothing to replace financially.

verdictSummary: A Schulte table is a shuffled grid of numbers, a timer, and a click handler. There is no data moat, no account system worth having, and no server component that matters: the entire product is one page of state. An agent can produce a working version with multiple grid sizes, letter and mixed color modes, a center fixation dot, and local best times in a single sitting. What you do not get for free is the polish, the mode variety accumulated over time, and the mild accountability of a site that already ranks for the term. If you actually do the exercise daily, a local copy is strictly better because it loads instantly and never shows you an ad mid drill.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a shuffled grid, times how long you take to click every cell in the correct order, counts mistakes, and stores your best runs per grid size in localStorage.
requirements: A text editor and a way to open a local HTML file
No server, no accounts, no API keys
whatYouLose: Mode variety that took someone years to accumulate: rotating grids, moving cells, color pairs, alphabet mixes, exotic sizes
Cross device history, since localStorage does not follow you to your phone
Any sense of how your times compare to other people
Layout that has actually been tuned for small screens and thumb reach
Someone else deciding what the next useful drill is, so your version stays whatever you built on day one
moatNotes: The real asset is search ranking for a term people type once out of curiosity, plus enough mode variety that casual users never feel the need to look elsewhere. Neither survives contact with a determined afternoon.
whyPeopleStillPay: Mostly they do not pay, they just land on it from a search result about speed reading and use it twice. The value on offer is zero friction: no download, no file to keep, works on the phone you are holding. A self built version wins only if you are the kind of person who will genuinely open a local page every morning, which is a much smaller group than the number of people who bookmark one.
notes: One of the rare entries where the honest answer is that the app is a weekend project someone already shipped and ranked.
prompt:
Build a single file Schulte table trainer as a local web app. No build step, no framework, no backend, no accounts, no analytics, no external requests of any kind.

Stack: one index.html containing HTML, CSS in a style tag, and vanilla JavaScript in a script tag. It must work by double clicking the file.

Core loop:
- Render a square grid of shuffled cells. Grid size selectable: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 per side.
- The user clicks cells in the required order. Correct clicks dim the cell and advance the target. Wrong clicks flash the cell red and increment a mistake counter, without advancing.
- A timer starts on the first click and stops when the last cell is cleared. Show elapsed time live, one decimal place.
- On completion show time, mistakes, and average seconds per cell, plus a Restart button.

Modes, all selectable from a single row of buttons:
- Numbers ascending, 1 to n squared.
- Numbers descending.
- Letters ascending, wrapping past 26 with A1, B1 style labels if needed.
- Red and black mix: red numbers ascending and black numbers descending, alternating turns, both sets sized to half the grid.
- Shuffle on hit: reshuffle all remaining cells after each correct click.

Discipline aids:
- A fixed dot at the exact center of the grid, toggleable, since the whole point is peripheral vision.
- Optional hide mode where cell text only renders on hover is explicitly out of scope. Do not add it.

Persistence: store the best time and lowest mistake count per grid size and mode in localStorage. Show a compact personal bests table under the grid. Include a Clear stats button with a confirm.

Input: full mouse and touch support, and number key entry is out of scope.

Styling: dark background, high contrast monospace cells, square cells that scale to viewport so the grid never scrolls on a phone. Keep it under 400 lines total. No dependencies, no fonts loaded from a CDN.

Out of scope: user accounts, leaderboards, sound, animations beyond a 100ms flash, service worker, README beyond three lines.
